subject: Renewal: surge buffer addendum and MSA alignment
messages:
From: Jared Mills <jared.mills@peaklytics.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal + surge buffer ask

Hi Kimberly & Ben,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. PeakLytics is supportive of the 12‑month renewal at the proposed rates, but a couple of asks came up from our infra team: they want a short-term "surge buffer" to cover unexpected campaign spikes for Q3 (we estimate ~15% additional token throughput for 6 weeks).

Can Redwood provide an addendum that: 1) specifies a temporary capacity buffer (billing as consumption over committed units), 2) clarifies how that buffer interacts with SLA credits, and 3) includes an explicit end date for the buffer? Procurement also requested to see the latest Order Form v3 and a side-by-side redline of any MSA changes.

I attached the updated PeakLytics forecast and a spreadsheet with sample surge curves. Let me know if we should route this to legal or if you can draft an addendum we can sign quickly.

Thanks,
Jared
Jared Mills
Head of Engineering, PeakLytics
Attachments: PeakLytics_Forecast_Q3.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), surge-profiles.csv (data stub)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jared Mills <jared.mills@peaklytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal + surge buffer ask

Thanks Jared — this is straightforward to handle and we can get a minimal addendum drafted. Proposed plan:

- Redwood drafts a short addendum ("Surge Buffer Addendum") that:
  * Defines a temporary capacity band (e.g., +15% of baseline committed tokens) for a defined 6‑week window starting on the first activated surge day.
  * States that overage charges during the buffer will be billed at the standard overage rate (or an agreed uplift) and that buffer-triggered capacity will not change the committed baseline.
  * Clarifies SLA interplay: credits remain based on baseline SLOs; we can include targeted credit language for full outages during the buffer period if helpful.
  * Auto-expires at the window end unless parties agree in writing to extend.

- I will send an internal redline of Exhibit C (capacity schedule) alongside the addendum. Ben — can you and Markus do a quick legal ops check on the billing language and any procurement constraints? Marissa, can you prepare the Order Form v3 with the renewal term and the optional buffer line item so Jared's team can quickly approve the math?

If that works, I'll draft the addendum and share a redline by EOD Monday.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | kimberly.park@redwood.com
Attachment stubs: none

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2026 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal proposal + surge buffer ask — redline guidance

Kimberly / Markus — forwarding Jared's note. Quick legal ops take below (high level):

- Billing model: prefer explicit overage rate and a cap on total chargeable overage during the buffer window to avoid surprise invoices. Suggest language: "Overage charges for surge buffer usage will be billed at X per token, capped at Y% of the monthly committed spend for the buffer window."

- SLA / credits: recommend clarifying that SLA credits remain calculated on committed baseline throughput; however, for material service degradations during the buffer window, include a discretionary supplemental credit clause limited to direct usage charges from the buffer window (so we don't expand liability).

- Termination/extension: add a one‑time mutual extension option with 7 days written notice before the buffer window end. Keep addendum short and non-amending-to-MSA unless absolutely necessary.

Marissa — we'll need the order form line item names aligned to these definitions so finance can map revenue recognition.

Ben
Ben Carter
VP, Contracts & Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
